name: The Met Cloisters
address: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
tagline: Medieval Europe at the northern tip of Manhattan. Same ticket as the Met.
description: The Met's medieval branch, built from fragments of five French abbeys reassembled in Fort Tryon Park. Houses the Unicorn Tapestries and Romanesque cloisters in a setting more contemplative than anything else in Manhattan.
review_long:
The Cloisters were built in the 1930s using stone from five medieval French abbeys, shipped to New York and reassembled on the high ground of Fort Tryon Park. The building feels older than anything actually in Manhattan should — the cloisters around the herb garden, the Romanesque chapel, the Unicorn Tapestries hanging in their own purpose-lit gallery.

Included on the Met's three-day ticket. Easiest from the A train to 190th.
